minutes.headline: Planning Board declined to require extra stormwater treatment and approved Unitil's Electric Avenue site plan.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed two ANR plans, accepted a prescriptive easement finding for Fire Road 16, and approved a Walmart outdoor seasonal sales area. The main item was the continued Unitil site plan review at 357 Electric Avenue, where a storm scepter request from Conservation was debated and rejected, and the site plan approved with conditions. The board then voted on the site plan zoning articles and parking design standards, endorsed a rezoning petition for 1026 Northfield Road, approved minutes, and heard committee reports.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted not to require Unitil to re-engineer stormwater treatment at 357 Electric Avenue, accepting the peer review engineer's finding.
The board then approved the Unitil site development plan with conditions, including set construction hours and compliance with other boards' conditions.
The board voted to support a petition to rezone 1026 Northfield Road from Recreation to Residence A; no public comment was offered.
The board accepted site plan approval and off street parking design zoning articles and a change in district types, then closed the public hearing.
The board endorsed two ANR plans, agreed a prescriptive easement exists on Fire Road 16, and approved a Walmart outdoor seasonal sales area.

why_it_matters: The stormwater vote settles whether added treatment is required at the Unitil outfall, which drains toward nearby lakes and wetlands; Conservation members and residents had pressed for it, and the cost of extra treatment was disputed.
The site plan, parking and district-type articles and the Northfield Road rezoning are zoning changes that residents may be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Next meeting March 28, with Prospect Street and Highfield on the agenda and a rules and regulations review to follow.
Town Meeting on May 7; traffic count location requests are due May 1, for discussion at the first April meeting.
